gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the AC180's solar input is capped at 10 A (500 W, 12–60 V, DC7909 port). Because watts = volts × amps, the panel string has to run near 50 V to reach the full 500 W, and its open-circuit voltage still has to stay under the 60 V limit. Adding a second panel in parallel, the way Trek4Tech suggests, raises the current but not the voltage, so it hits the 10 A cap.
standout_why: I read the three rival pages ChatGPT cited or ranked: StormWatts (bundle-vs-separate price math), GetWattLogic (cited) and Trek4Tech, plus our own page. StormWatts gives only wattage caps ('500 W' on the AC180) and says to 'check Voc, amps, and connectors'. It gives no current limit and says nothing about series or parallel wiring. GetWattLogic names MC4/XT60 and MPPT but gives no voltage or amp figures. Trek4Tech gives an '11–60V' window and wattage caps, but says a second panel should be 'wired in parallel' and never mentions an amp ceiling. Our page says only 'check the panel's open-circuit voltage against the station's input window and the connector'. None of them gives a current cap in amps, explains the volts × amps limit, or names the AC180's DC7909 input.
decides: Buying separately to save money on the AC180 only works if the shopper also plans the wiring. With a 10 A ceiling, a single 200 W panel is fine. Two panels in parallel are still held to 10 A, so the second panel adds little. To get toward the 500 W input, the panels have to go in series, at about 50 V with an open-circuit voltage under 60 V. BLUETTI's 2×200 W kit is $65 cheaper than the same parts bought separately ($1,232 vs $499 + 2 × $399 = $1,297, read today). A third-party panel also needs an MC4-to-DC7909 cable. This supports our page's verdict: the kit is the safe default, and a third-party panel saves money only for a buyer who checks the 10 A and 60 V limits. Note: today's AC180+200W kit price is $769 (compare-at $899), not the $729 on our current page.

findings.label: Minimum voltage for full 500 W solar input (arithmetic)
findings.value: ≈50 V at the 10 A cap; Voc must stay ≤60 V
findings.source_title: Bluetti AC180 - Portable Power Station Manual (ManualsLib)
findings.note: 500 W ÷ 10 A = 50 V. A string with a 20 V operating point delivers at most 20 V × 10 A = 200 W, however many panels are wired in parallel. Only a series string near 50 V can reach 500 W, and its cold-weather Voc must stay under 60 V.
